title: FAUST. VII. Detection of a Hot Corino in the Prototypical Warm Carbon-chain Chemistry Source IRAS 15398-3359
question: Whether a hot corino exists in the vicinity of the protostar in the prototypical warm carbon-chain chemistry (WCCC) source IRAS 15398-3359.

what.value: Systemic velocity of 5.5 km s^-1, disk radius of 40 au, and protostellar mass of 0.007 +0.004/-0.003 M_odot

evidence.quote: The protostellar mass is estimated to be as small as 0.007$^{+0.004}_{-0.003}$ $M_\odot$ from the Keplerian rotation, and the disk mass between 0.006 $M_\odot$ and 0.001 $M_\odot$ from 1.2 mm dust continuum emission, assuming the dust temperature of 20 K and 100 K, respectively (cite: Okoda et al.(2018)).

We here employ the systemic velocity of this protostellar source of 5.5 km s$^{-1}$, which is previously reported on the basis of the Keplerian rotation motion of the disk component by (cite: Okoda et al.(2018)).
A Keplerian disk, with the radius of 40 au in the SO emission, has been reported by (cite: Okoda et al.(2018)).

external_data.citation: Okoda et al. (2018) (cite: Okoda et al.(2018))

evidence.quote: The bolometric luminosity of IRAS 15398$-$3359 is 1.8 $L_\odot$(cite: Jorgensen et al.(2013)), which is similar to that of B335 and twice that of CB68.

external_data.citation: Jørgensen et al. (2013) (cite: Jorgensen et al.(2013))

what.value: Column densities and abundance ratios of CH3OH, CH2DOH, and CH3OCHO for comparison sources (B335, L483, CB68, L1551 IRS5, NGC 1333 IRAS2A, IRAS 16293-2422B)

evidence.quote: We summarize and compare the abundances of CH$_2$DOH and CH$_3$OCHO relative to CH$_3$OH among low-mass protostars having a hot corino in Table 3.

The ratios for the other sources, CB68 (0.09$^{+0.07}_{-0.03}$) (cite: Imai et al.(2022)) and L1551 IRS5 (0.033$\pm$0.002) (cite: Bianchi et al.(2020)), and IRAS 16293-2422B (0.026$^{+0.008}_{-0.007}$) (cite: Jorgensen et al.(2018)), are within the range of the ratios in IRAS 15398$-$3359.

recipe.goal: Measure 1.2 mm continuum peak position, intensity, and deconvolved size
recipe.method: 2D Gaussian fit to the 1.2 mm dust continuum image
assumptions: Gaussian spatial distribution for the central continuum peak

recipe.goal: Extract spectra, identify CH3OH lines, and map high-excitation CH3OH emission
recipe.method: Extract spectra toward the 0.2'' (~30 au) area around the continuum peak and toward the continuum peak position; identify CH3OH lines above 3 sigma; create stacked integrated-intensity map of blueshifted (-0.2 to 5.0 km s^-1) and redshifted (5.8 to 10.6 km s^-1) components for the three CH3OH lines with E_u > 400 K; fit Gaussian profiles to the 9 CH3OH lines toward the continuum peak to measure peak intensities and line widths
key_parameters: Blueshifted velocity range: -0.2 km s^-1 to 5.0 km s^-1; Redshifted velocity range: 5.8 km s^-1 to 10.6 km s^-1

recipe.goal: Derive rotation temperature, column density, and beam filling factor of CH3OH
recipe.method: Simultaneous non-linear least-squares fit of source rotation temperature (T), column density (N), and beam filling factor (f) to the observed peak intensities and line widths of the 9 CH3OH lines using radiative transfer equations (1) and (2) under LTE
key_parameters: T_cmb = 2.7 K; simulated spectrum uses systemic velocity 2.9 km s^-1 and average line width 3.4 km s^-1
assumptions: Local thermodynamic equilibrium (LTE) with a single rotation temperature

recipe.goal: Detect CH2DOH and CH3OCHO lines and derive their column densities and abundance ratios relative to CH3OH
recipe.method: Measure integrated intensities of CH2DOH (at 234.471 GHz) and blended CH3OCHO features (at 234.5 GHz and 247.1 GHz), evaluate column densities using LTE equations (1) and (2), and compute abundance ratios relative to CH3OH
key_parameters: Line width fixed to average CH3OH line width of 3.4 km s^-1
assumptions: LTE, and rotation temperature and beam filling factor are identical to those derived for CH3OH (T = 119 +20/-26 K, f = 0.018 +0.005/-0.003)
